title: Operator Auxiliaries: Taskification, Safe Dry-Run Simulation, and Synthetic Safeguards
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Convert a curated set of operator scripts and ad-hoc admin utilities into first-class, idempotent Linear tasks with a safe dry-run simulator and synthetic safeguards so first-line support can execute common remediations without escalation. Background: we currently have many handoff scripts and runbooks that are brittle, environment-sensitive, and missing telemetry. This ticket scopes a minimal viable task architecture plus a simulation harness that executes tasks in a sandbox using synthetic inputs (fixtures) and validates side effects are idempotent or roll-backable. Deliverables: (1) task adapter library (python/ts) for wrapping scripts, (2) dry-run simulator service with fixture registry, (3) policy layer for gating destructive actions, (4) telemetry hooks and action provenance recording, (5) basic CLI and Console integration surface for daily ops. Outcomes: reduced mean time to remediate for 80% of frequent incidents, lower escalation rate, and clear audit trail for compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Create a task adapter library that can wrap bash/python/ruby admin scripts and expose typed inputs and outputs
Dry-run simulator runs tasks against fixture set and produces a deterministic report with potential side effects flagged
All wrapped tasks include provenance headers (actor, task-id, fixture-id) and emit structured telemetry to ops-telemetry
Policy layer prevents any task flagged as 'destructive' from running in non-approved contexts; admin override requires two-person confirmation
CLI command 'ops-task run --dry-run <task>' and Console button with dry-run preview are implemented
Documentation and 3 runbook examples converted and validated by oncall in rehearsals
steps: Design task adapter interface and IDL for typed parameters
Implement adapter for python scripts (lib + examples)
Prototype dry-run harness that can stub external systems and capture API calls
Integrate policy gating and implement two-person override flow
Add structured telemetry and event schema to ops-telemetry
Ship CLI surface and Console integration with preview pane
Run 3 rehearsals with oncall and iterate on failing cases
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: initially use fixture stubbing rather than full environment replay to reduce infra cost; this will miss timing/latency issues but catches logic-level regressions.
Decision: adopt a small, opinionated IDL instead of full protobuf generation to speed adoption; revisit if third-party consumers appear.
Risk: wrapping legacy scripts may surface secrets in logs; mitigated by redaction hooks and KMS-enforced secret fetch patterns.
Performance: simulation runs will be scheduled on low-priority infra and are not on the critical path for real remediations.
Operational burden: add TTL-based fixture cleanup and quota for on-demand simulations to avoid runaway costs.
